overview: Togo is a narrow country in West Africa, between Ghana and Benin, with a short coast on the Gulf of Guinea. Its capital and largest city is Lomé. Togo became independent from France in 1960. French is the official language, and Togo is an important producer of phosphate.

geography.text: Togo stretches more than 500 kilometres inland but is never much more than 150 kilometres wide. The coast has lagoons and sandy beaches, with plateaus behind. A range of hills and mountains crosses the country from south-west to north-east, and the north is savanna.

history.text: Ewe and other peoples lived in the region, which was part of the slave-trading 'Slave Coast'. Germany made Togoland a colony in 1884. After the First World War it was split between Britain and France; the British part joined Ghana. French Togo became independent in 1960. The Gnassingbé family has ruled since 1967.

events.title: Split
events.text: Britain and France take the colony.

events.title: British part joins Ghana
events.text: British Togoland votes to join the Gold Coast.

events.title: Eyadéma
events.text: Gnassingbé Eyadéma takes power for 38 years.
